ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=6$, $AC=BC=5$. $\triangle ABC$ is rotated clockwise around point $A$ to obtain $\triangle ADE$, with the angle of rotation being $\alpha$ ($0^\circ<\alpha<180^\circ$), where point $B$ corresponds to point $D$, and point $C$ corresponds to point $E$. When the angle between the lines $AB$ and $AD$ equals $\angle ACB$, what is the length of $BE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, connect BD,

$\because$ $AC=BC$

$\therefore$ $\angle CAB=\angle CBA$

Based on the property of rotation,

$\angle CBA=\angle ADE$,

$AD=AB$

$\therefore$ $\angle ADB=\angle ABD$

$\because$ $\angle ACB=\angle DAB$

$\therefore$ $\angle CAB=\angle CBA=\angle ADE=\angle ADB=\angle ABD$

$\therefore$ $D$, $E$, $B$ are collinear

$\because$ $\frac{AC}{AD}=\frac{BC}{AB}$,

$\angle ACB=\angle DAB$

$\therefore$ $\triangle ACB\sim \triangle DAB$

$\therefore$ $\frac{AC}{AD}=\frac{AB}{DB}$, thus

$\frac{5}{6}=\frac{6}{DB}$

Solving gives

$DB=\frac{36}{5}$

$\therefore$ $BE=DB-DE=\frac{36}{5}-5=\boxed{\frac{11}{5}}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A is on the left side, B is on the right side, and AB is approximately horizontal; C is above, forming the original triangle ABC with A and B; the rotated point D is at the lower right, E is at the upper right, and AD, AE, DE are drawn in the figure, and BD can be connected according to the problem meaning. A is the center of rotation, AB is rotated to AD, and C and B respectively correspond to E and D. According to the relative positions in the figure, after connecting BD, the directions of DB and DE starting from D can be compared. Reasoning: Let γ=∠ACB. Because AC=BC=5, the original triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle, and ∠CAB=∠CBA. The problem gives that the angle between the straight lines AB and AD is equal to ∠ACB, therefore ∠DAB=γ. By the property of rotation, AD=AB=6, DE=BC=5, and ∠ADE=∠ABC. Also because AD=AB, triangle ABD is an isosceles triangle, whose vertex angle ∠DAB=γ, therefore the base angles ∠ADB=∠ABD=(180°−γ)/2. In the original triangle, ∠CAB=∠CBA=(180°−γ)/2, so ∠ADB=∠ABD=∠ABC=∠ADE. From the positions in the figure, it can be known that DB and DE are on the same side of D and correspond to the same direction, therefore D, E, B are collinear, and E is between D and B. Looking again at triangles ACB and DAB: AC/AD=5/6, BC/AB=5/6, and the included angle ∠ACB=∠DAB=γ, so ΔACB ∼ ΔDAB. The corresponding sides give AC/AD=AB/DB, that is, 5/6=6/DB, solving gives DB=36/5. Also DE=5, so BE=DB−DE=36/5−5=11/5.
